title: ProteinGPT: Multimodal LLM for Protein Property Prediction and Structure Understanding

live_model.id_in_text: OpenAI o3-mini (also GPT-4-turbo, GPT-4o; snapshots not stated)
live_model.evidence: Sec. 4.2.3: 'we prepended the protein's FASTA sequence to the prompt'; Table 4: 'GPT-4-turbo 0.049 0.001 0.049 0.048' / 'OpenAI o3-mini 0.072 0.007 0.072 0.073' (R-1 R-2 R-L R-Lsum)

prompt.location: Baseline prompt = question with the FASTA sequence prepended (Sec. 4.2.3); exact wording not printed; ProteinGPT instruction prompts in the Appendix

claim.metric: ROUGE-L on protein QA test questions
claim.location: Table 4, row OpenAI o3-mini, column R-L (1,025 questions from 35 test proteins)

data.source: ProteinGPT dataset (132,092 proteins with QA pairs) and code at https://github.com/ProteinGPT/ProteinGPT; test proteins from RCSB PDB

notes: Baseline numbers are secondary (the subject is the fine-tuned ProteinGPT); o3-mini / GPT-4-turbo snapshots are not stated and the exact 1,025-question subset is not identified. GPT-4-turbo row: R-L 0.049.

resolution.plan: The 1,025 questions are an unlisted random sample of 35 proteins (28-30 questions each) from the 160-protein test split (Sec. 4.2.1). Draw a seeded random sample of 35 proteins from the released test split (or the released dataset's test proteins if no split file), keep all their questions, prepend the FASTA sequence to each question (Sec. 4.2.3), query o3-mini, and compare ROUGE-L against the reference answers at the set level (0.072).
resolution.approximation: Different 35-protein sample; prompt formatting and o3-mini reasoning effort unstated; the paper's 3,508-pair test set is itself described as randomly selected.
